A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PENG-CDE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated material and removed checklist content.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic simulations, real-world benchmark evaluations, sampling-robustness experiments, and learned fusion-weight analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds wealth and opinion dynamics evaluations, statistical analyses, and graph-size runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The documented PENG-CDE procedure is unchanged: Equations 5–7 retain the equivariant fusion and dynamic node-feature extension. The source-target identification construction also matches between v1 Appendix F.5 and v2 Appendix G.5.

E1.justification: v2 adds wealth/personal-capital and opinion dynamics across the four graph families in Appendix F, substantially extending the synthetic evaluation into economic and social dynamics. Heat diffusion, gene regulation, SIR classification, and all four real-world datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DCRNN, STIDGCN, ASTGCN, and STG-NCDE to both heat-diffusion and gene-regulation comparisons. Although present elsewhere in v1, they substantially broaden these previously GNODE/GN-CDE-centred comparisons. Tables 2–3 retain their comparator sets; the new real-world rank diagrams additionally include ConstVectorField.

E3.justification: Appendix I introduces a runtime protocol varying graph size over 128, 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 nodes and measuring seconds per training epoch. Existing experiments retain their stated splits, sampling procedures, training budgets, and hyperparameters. The new explanation of expected topology-change counts does not change the sampling design.

E4.justification: Appendices H–I add analyses of comparative statistical significance across the experimental families and runtime scaling with node count. The existing fusion-weight analysis moves from Appendix H/Table 9 to Section 4.3/Table 4 with unchanged weights; the SIR oversampling and irregularity experiments are also retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds global Friedman testing, conditional aligned-Friedman post-hoc comparisons, and critical-difference diagrams in Appendix H. v1 reported confidence intervals and standard deviations without these tests. Existing uncertainty formats and ten-seed real-world averaging remain; an increase in run counts is not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline scores in Table 1, wealth/opinion results in Table 5, rank summaries in Figures 3–5, and timings in Table 11. At 2048 nodes, reported epoch times are 1.50 seconds for PENG-CDE versus 9.15 for Pre Mult GN-CDE. Existing Table 1 entries, Tables 2–3, and fusion weights are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix G.2 adds mathematical definitions of wealth and thresholded opinion dynamics in Equations 26–27, including the threshold function. The main equivariance definitions, Theorem 3.1, Proposition 3.2, and supporting proofs in Appendices A–E remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about equivariant projection, parameter efficiency, temporal and spatial equivariance, improved prediction, and state-of-the-art TGB-genre performance.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the snapshot results by reporting no statistically significant model differences in Appendix H. It explains quadratic memory requirements and attributes the sparse-matrix bottleneck primarily to JAX, while distinguishing runtime scaling from memory limits. It also refines the relevance of time-warp equivariance and interpretations of the retained fusion weights.

D1.justification: The advertised code location changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository. v2 adds simulator equations and per-epoch timing information, and explicitly identifies additive GN-CDE fusion in the TGB comparison. Existing software, hardware, and hyperparameter disclosures are retained; the fusion footnote does not establish an experimental reconfiguration.

R1.justification: v2 distinguishes the original GN-CDE preprint from its later journal version and discusses that version’s additional fusion matrix and nonlinear fusion. It acknowledges comparable TGB performance from the latter. This changes positioning relative to an existing work; the broader related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition is retained. Targeted changes expand the time-warp motivation and limitations discussion, move and elaborate the fusion analysis into Section 4.3, remove the NeurIPS checklist, and add acknowledgements and publication information. Appendix labels change to accommodate the additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds three multipanel critical-difference figures and new wealth/opinion and runtime tables, substantially expanding the visual evidence. Table 1 gains baseline blocks. The fusion-weight table is relocated and reformatted as Table 4; Figures 1–2 retain their plotted content despite surrounding layout changes.

improvement.justification: Broader synthetic comparisons and measured runtime scaling strengthen the empirical assessment, while Appendix H acknowledges nonsignificant snapshot-dataset differences. Reporting problems limit these gains: the new wealth equation contains a self-cancelling interaction term, and several variants in the statistical diagrams lack explanation. With the original method, proofs, and headline results retained, the additions support a modest net improvement.
